title: Singapore Budget 2026 statement and motion to approve FY2026/2027 financial policy
what_it_is: A Budget statement by the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance moving a motion for Parliament to approve the Government's financial policy for FY2026/2027, followed by adjournment of the debate.
why_it_matters: The Budget sets out changes including a 40% Corporate Income Tax rebate for companies, a higher Local Qualifying Salary from $1,600 to $1,800, CPF top-ups of up to $1,500 for Singaporeans aged 50 and above with lower retirement savings, $500 Child LifeSG Credits, and cost-of-living payments of $200 to $400. It also raises Employment Pass and S Pass qualifying salaries from January 2027 and increases tobacco excise duty by 20% with effect from today.

key_points.point: Parliament is asked to approve the Government's financial policy for FY2026/2027.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: That Parliament approves the financial policy of the Government for the Financial Year 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027.

key_points.point: Growth is projected at 2% to 4% and inflation at 1% to 2%.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: Growth is therefore projected at 2% to 4%; with inflation at 1% to 2%.

key_points.point: A 40% Corporate Income Tax rebate will be provided in Year of Assessment 2026, with a minimum benefit of $1,500 and a cap of $30,000 per company.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: I will provide a 40% Corporate Income Tax rebate in the Year of Assessment 2026. Every active company that employed at least one local employee last year will receive a minimum benefit of $1,500. The total benefit for each company will be capped at $30,000.

key_points.point: Support levels for internationalisation grant schemes will be enhanced to up to 70% for SMEs and up to 50% for non-SMEs.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: We will enhance the support levels for grant schemes that support companies to internationalise – up to 70% for small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and up to 50% for non-SMEs.

key_points.point: More qualifying activities will be eligible for automatic Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation claims, and the cap will be raised to $400,000.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: We will allow more qualifying activities to be eligible for such automatic tax deduction claims and raise the cap to $400,000.

key_points.point: $37 billion will be invested under the RIE2030 plan.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: That is why we will invest $37 billion under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise, or RIE2030 plan.

key_points.point: $1 billion will be set aside to enhance Startup SG Equity and expand it to growth-stage companies.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: I will set aside $1 billion to enhance Startup SG Equity, and expand its scope to cover growth-stage companies.

key_points.point: A second $1.5 billion tranche of the Anchor Fund will be launched.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: I will therefore launch a second $1.5 billion tranche of the Anchor Fund.

key_points.point: The Equity Market Development Programme will be expanded with a $1.5 billion top-up to the Financial Sector Development Fund.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: To build on this momentum, I will expand the programme, with a $1.5 billion top-up to the Financial Sector Development Fund.

key_points.point: National AI Missions will focus on advanced manufacturing, connectivity, finance and healthcare.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: We will focus on four sectors: advanced manufacturing, connectivity, finance and healthcare.

key_points.point: A new National AI Council, chaired by the Prime Minister, will provide strategic direction for Singapore's AI agenda.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: We will therefore establish a new National AI Council, which I will chair, to provide strategic direction and to drive Singapore's AI agenda.

key_points.point: A new Champions of AI programme will support firms seeking comprehensive AI transformation.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: So, we will launch a new Champions of AI programme to support firms with the ambition to use AI to comprehensively transform their business.

key_points.point: The Enterprise Innovation Scheme will include AI expenditures for Years of Assessment 2027 and 2028, capped at $50,000 per Year of Assessment.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: We will expand the scheme to include AI expenditures as a qualifying activity, for the Years of Assessment 2027 and 2028, capped at $50,000 per Year of Assessment.

key_points.point: The Productivity Solutions Grant will be expanded to support a wider range of digital and AI-enabled solutions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: We will expand the PSG to support a wider range of digital and AI-enabled solutions, so that every firm, regardless of size, can access tools that help them work smarter and compete more effectively.

key_points.point: A larger AI park will be established at One-North.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: We will build on this pilot and establish a larger AI park at One-North.

key_points.point: Singaporeans who take up selected AI training courses will receive six months of free access to premium AI tools.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: we will provide Singaporeans who take up selected AI training courses six months of free access to premium AI tools.

key_points.point: The Local Qualifying Salary for full-time local employees will be raised from $1,600 to $1,800.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: We will raise the LQS for full-time local employees from $1,600 to $1,800.

key_points.point: PWCS co-funding support will be raised from 20% to 30% this year.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: We will raise the PWCS co-funding support for this year, from 20% to 30%.

key_points.point: The PWCS will be extended for two more years, to 2028.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: We will also extend the PWCS for two more years, to 2028.

key_points.point: SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore will be merged into a new statutory board jointly overseen by MOE and MOM.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: We will merge SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore into a new statutory board jointly overseen by MOE and MOM.

key_points.point: From next month, the Mid-Career Training Allowance will be extended to part-time training.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: From next month, the Mid-Career Training Allowance will be extended to those who take up not just full-time, but also part-time training.

key_points.point: The Senior Employment Credit will be extended to end-2027.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: we will extend the Senior Employment Credit to end-2027, to support employers who continue to employ senior workers.

key_points.point: The Employment Pass minimum qualifying salary for new applicants will be raised from $5,600 to $6,000 from January 2027.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: We will raise the Employment Pass (EP) minimum qualifying salary for new applicants from $5,600 to $6,000 from January 2027.

key_points.point: From January 2027, the minimum qualifying salary for new S Pass applicants will be raised from $3,300 to $3,600.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: From January 2027, the minimum qualifying salary for new S Pass applicants will be raised from $3,300 to $3,600.

key_points.point: For the Marine and Process sectors, Work Permit levies for basic skilled workers will be raised by $100 and $150 respectively.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: For the Marine and Process sectors, levies for basic skilled workers will be raised by $100 and $150, respectively.

key_points.point: Another $500 in Child LifeSG Credits will be provided for each Singaporean child aged 12 and below.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: This year, we will provide another $500 in Child LifeSG Credits to families for each Singaporean child aged 12 and below.

key_points.point: From the start of next year, means-tested preschool subsidies will be extended by raising the monthly household income threshold to $15,000.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: From the start of next year, we will extend means-tested preschool subsidies to more families, by raising the monthly household income threshold to $15,000.

key_points.point: A new ComLink+ payout of $500 per quarter will be provided for families who commit to work with family coaches and take active steps to make progress.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: First, we will provide a new payout of $500 per quarter for all ComLink+ families who make a commitment to work with family coaches and take active steps to make progress.

key_points.point: The Long-Term Care Support Fund will be topped up by $400 million to fund additional subsidies.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: I will top up the Long-Term Care Support Fund by $400 million to fund the additional subsidies.

key_points.point: A CPF top-up of up to $1,500 will be provided for Singaporeans aged 50 and above with CPF retirement savings below the Basic Retirement Sum.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: First, we will provide a CPF top-up of up to $1,500 for Singaporeans aged 50 and above, and with CPF retirement savings below the Basic Retirement Sum.

key_points.point: The next step of planned CPF contribution rate increases for senior workers will proceed in 2027.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: Second, we will proceed with the next step of planned CPF contribution rate increases for senior workers in 2027.

key_points.point: Participation in the new CPF investment scheme will be voluntary.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: Participation in the new investment scheme will be voluntary.

key_points.point: A Cost-of-Living Special Payment of $200 to $400 in cash will be provided to Singaporean adults earning up to $100,000 in Assessable Income and who do not own more than one property.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: First, I will provide a Cost-of-Living Special Payment, comprising $200 to $400 in cash, to Singaporean adults earning up to $100,000 in Assessable Income and who do not own more than one property.

key_points.point: Eligible HDB households will receive 1.5 times the regular amount of U-Save rebates, or up to $570 this financial year.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: Eligible HDB households will receive 1.5 times the regular amount of U-Save rebates, or up to $570 this financial year.

key_points.point: Another $500 in CDC Vouchers will be provided to all Singaporean households in January 2027.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: I will provide another $500 in Community Development Council (CDC) Vouchers

key_points.point: Defence spending is expected to be kept at about 3% of GDP for now.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: For now, we expect to keep defence spending at about 3% of GDP.

key_points.point: The carbon tax has been raised to $45 per tonne for this year and next, with a plan to reach $50 to $80 per tonne by 2030.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: The tax has just been raised to $45 per tonne for this year and next, and the plan is to reach $50 to $80 per tonne by 2030.

key_points.point: The solar deployment target will be raised to three gigawatt-peak by 2030.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: We will therefore raise the target to three gigawatt-peak by 2030.

key_points.point: Singapore remains committed to achieving 100% cleaner vehicles by 2040.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: In transport, we remain committed to achieving 100% cleaner vehicles by 2040.

key_points.point: The PARF rebate will be reduced by 45 percentage points.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: Therefore, I will reduce the PARF rebate by 45 percentage points.

key_points.point: Tobacco excise duty will be increased by 20% across all tobacco products with effect from today.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: I will implement a 20% increase in tobacco excise duty across all tobacco products with effect from today.

key_points.point: FY2025 is expected to end with a surplus of $15.1 billion, or 1.9% of GDP.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: Therefore, I expect to end FY2025 with a surplus of $15.1 billion, or 1.9% of GDP.

key_points.point: FY2026 is expected to have a smaller surplus of $8.5 billion, or 1% of GDP.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: For FY2026, I expect a smaller surplus of $8.5 billion, or 1% of GDP.

key_points.point: The Top-up Tax under Pillar Two of BEPS will be implemented.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: On the revenue side, we will proceed with the implementation of the Top-up Tax under Pillar Two of Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS).

key_points.point: The debate now stands adjourned.
key_points.speaker: Mr Speaker
key_points.quote: In accordance with paragraph (1) of Standing Order No 89, the debate now stands adjourned.

key_points.point: The debate is to be resumed on Tuesday, 24 February 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: Tuesday, 24 February 2026, Sir.

what_happens_next: The debate stands adjourned and is to be resumed on Tuesday, 24 February 2026; several Ministers will provide more details at the Committee of Supply.
